newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RALLYING-FINN MAKINEN GRABS RALLY AUSTRALIA LEAD.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-FINN MAKINEN GRABS RALLY AUSTRALIA LEAD.

text.p: Finn Tommi Makinen, runaway leader of the World Championship, forged into a comfortable lead on the first day of Rally Australia, the seventh round of the series, on Saturday.
The Mitsubishi driver swept past early leader Carlos Sainz of Spain to build up an advantage of more than half a minute.
"I can go faster if I want, but it is a difficult rally and still there are a lot of long stages," said Makinen.
Ford driver Sainz came under mounting pressure from Swede Kenneth Eriksson and Britain's Colin McRae as the Subaru team made amends for a bad start.
Eriksson said an electronic problem that affected his car's four-wheel drive system slowed him on one stage, but he ended the just three seconds behind Sainz, who lost ground with a misfire.
"For us, it's not bad, but you should never be happy if you are not leading," Eriksson said.

World Champion McRae, desperate to finish after three accidents in his last four rallies, was not happy with his choice of tyres in the morning. "There's a lot of water in places and I can't afford to take any chances. It's not a place you can take risks normally and certainly not in my position," he said.
However, fastest times on two of the afternoon stages hinted that he could make a bigger impact during the rest of the rally.

Briton Richard Burns, driving the second Mitsubishi, was in fifth place after pulling clear of Belgian Bruno Thiry when the Ford driver ran into trouble with his handbrake which made the car difficult to drive on hairpins.
"I was in third place - I was in the running," Thiry lamented.
Italy's Piero Liatti received a nasty shock on his first visit to Australia, crashing into a kangaroo that jumped out in front of him when he was driving his Subaru with a jammed accelerator.
